sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在早上4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想去看看下一颗恒星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能几乎每年都是联盟里最棒的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的首字母开局词。

And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个平底锅就能做好的菜，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，陪伴您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，尊享特别优惠：nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Over the past week, what had begun as a smattering of pro-Palestinian protests on America's college campuses exploded into a nationwide movement.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一周里，最初在美国大学校园里零星出现的亲巴勒斯坦抗议活动，演变成了全国性的运动。

sentences.en: As students at dozens of universities held demonstrations, set up encampments, and at times, seized academic buildings.
sentences.zh: 几十所大学的学生举行了示威游行，搭起了帐篷营地，有时甚至占领了学术大楼。

sentences.en: In response, administrators at many of those colleges decided to crack down.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，许多大学的管理者决定采取严厉打击措施。

sentences.en: Calling in local police to carry out mass detentions and arrests.
sentences.zh: 召集当地警察进行大规模扣留和逮捕。

sentences.en: From Arizona State.
sentences.zh: 从亚利桑那州立大学。

sentences.en: In the name of the state of Arizona, I declare this gathering to be a violation of A.R.
sentences.zh: 以亚利桑那州政府的名义，我宣布这次集会违反了A.R.
13条款。

sentences.en: To the University of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 到佐治亚大学。

sentences.en: To City College of New York.
sentences.zh: 再到纽约市立学院。

sentences.en: As of Thursday, police had arrested 2,000 students on more than 40 campuses.
sentences.zh: 截至周四，警方已在40多个校园逮捕了2000名学生。

sentences.en: A situation so startling that President Biden could no longer ignore it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种如此令人震惊的局势，以至于拜登总统再也无法忽视它。

sentences.en: Look, it's basically a matter of fairness.
sentences.zh: 听着，这基本上是一个公平问题。

sentences.en: It's a matter of what's right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关乎正义的问题。

sentences.en: There's the right to protest, but not the right to cause chaos.
sentences.zh: 抗议的权利是有的，但没有制造混乱的权利。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Jonathan Wolfe and Peter Baker on a history-making week.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事乔纳森·沃尔夫和彼得·贝克将带我们回顾创造历史的一周。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jonathan, as this tumultuous week on college campuses comes to an end, it feels like the most extraordinary scenes played out on the campus of the University of California,
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，随着校园里这个动荡的一周接近尾声，感觉最不寻常的一幕似乎发生在加州大学

sentences.en: Los Angeles, where you have been reporting.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶分校，也就是你一直在进行报道的地方。

sentences.en: What is the story of how that protest started and ultimately became so explosive?
sentences.zh: 这场抗议是如何开始并最终变得如此具有爆发力的，背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: So, late last week, pro-Palestinian protesters set up an encampment at the University of California, Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 所以，在上周末晚些时候，亲巴勒斯坦抗议者在加州大学洛杉矶分校搭起了帐篷营地。

sentences.en: It was right in front of Royce Hall, which I don't know if you are familiar with UCLA, but it's like a very famous red brick building.
sentences.zh: 它就在罗伊斯大楼的正前方，我不知道你对加州大学洛杉矶分校熟不熟悉，但它是一座非常著名的红砖建筑。

sentences.en: It's like on all the brochures.
sentences.zh: 所有的宣传册上都有它。

sentences.en: And there was two things that like stood out about this encampment.
sentences.zh: 这个营地有两个非常引人注目的特点。

sentences.en: And the first thing was that they sort of barricaded the encampment.
sentences.zh: 首先是他们对营地进行了某种形式的防御工事化。

sentences.en: The encampment, complete with tents and barricades, has been set up in the middle of the Westwood campus.
sentences.zh: 这个配有帐篷和路障的营地，已经搭建在韦斯特伍德校园的中央。

sentences.en: The protesters demand...
sentences.zh: 抗议者的诉求是……

sentences.en: They have, you know, metal grates, they had wooden pallets, and they sort of separated themselves from the campus.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们有金属栅栏，有木质托盘，他们实际上把自己和校园隔离开来。

sentences.en: This is kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 这其实挺有意思的。

sentences.en: They're controlling access, as we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 正如我们一直在讨论的，他们在控制出入权限。

sentences.en: They are trying to control who is allowed in, who is allowed out.
sentences.zh: 他们试图控制谁被允许进入，谁被允许离开。

sentences.en: They sort of policed the areas.
sentences.zh: 他们有点像是在那些区域进行巡逻治安。

sentences.en: They only would let people that were like part of their community, they said, inside.
sentences.zh: 他们说，只允许他们所谓自己社群内部的人进去。

sentences.en: I'm a UCLA student.
sentences.zh: 我是加州大学洛杉矶分校的学生。

sentences.en: I deserve to go here.
sentences.zh: 我有权来这里。

sentences.en: We pay tuition.
sentences.zh: 我们交了学费。

sentences.en: This is our school, and they're not letting me walk in.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的学校，而他们不让我走进去。

sentences.en: Well, I can't take it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我受不了了。

sentences.en: Will you let me go in?
sentences.zh: 你让我进去吗？

sentences.en: We're not engaging in that.
sentences.zh: 我们不参与这事。

sentences.en: Then you can move.
sentences.zh: 那你们可以走开。

sentences.en: Will you move?
sentences.zh: 你们会让开吗？

sentences.en: And the second thing that stood out about this camp was that it immediately attracted pro-Israel counter-protesters.
sentences.zh: 关于这个营地的第二个引人注目的特点是，它立刻吸引了亲以色列的反抗议者。

sentences.en: And what did the leadership of UCLA say about all of this, the encampment and these counter-protesters?
sentences.zh: 那么加州大学洛杉矶分校的领导层对这一切——包括营地和这些反抗议者——是怎么说的？

sentences.en: So the University of California's approach was pretty unique.
sentences.zh: 加州大学的做法非常独特。

sentences.en: They had a really hands-off approach, and they allowed the pro-Palestinian protesters to set up an encampment.
sentences.zh: 他们采取了一种非常放任的态度，允许亲巴勒斯坦抗议者搭建营地。

sentences.en: They allowed the counter-protesters to happen.
sentences.zh: 他们也允许反抗议活动的发生。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a public university, so anyone who wants to can just enter the campus.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一所公立大学，所以任何想来的人都可以直接进入校园。

sentences.en: So when do things start to escalate?
sentences.zh: 那么事情是什么时候开始升级的呢？

sentences.en: So there were definitely fights and scuffles through the weekend, but a turning point was really Sunday.
sentences.zh: 整个周末确实发生了一些冲突和争吵，但真正的转折点是周日。

sentences.en: When this group called the Israeli-American Council, they're a non-profit organization,
sentences.zh: 当时一个名为“以色列-美国委员会”的非营利组织，

sentences.en: organized a rally on campus, the Israeli-American Council has really been against these pro-Palestinian protests.
sentences.zh: 在校园里组织了一场集会。以色列-美国委员会一直反对这些亲巴勒斯坦的抗议活动。

sentences.en: They say that they're anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 他们称这些抗议是反犹太主义的。

sentences.en: So this non-profit group sets up a stage with a screen really just a few yards from the pro-Palestinian encampment.
sentences.zh: 于是这个非营利组织搭起了一个带有屏幕的舞台，距离亲巴勒斯坦营地只有短短几码远。

sentences.en: We are grateful that this past Friday, the University of California stated that they will continue to oppose any calls for boycott and divestment from Israel.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢加州大学在上周五发表声明，表示他们将继续反对任何抵制和撤资以色列的呼吁。

sentences.en: And they host speakers, and they held prayers.
sentences.zh: 他们邀请了演讲嘉宾，并举行了祈祷活动。

sentences.en: Jewish students, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 犹太学生们，你们并不孤单。

sentences.en: Oh, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 哦，你们并不孤单。

sentences.en: And then lots of other people start showing up, and the proximity between protesters and counter-protesters, and even some agitators,
sentences.zh: 然后许多其他人开始出现，抗议者与反抗议者之间的近距离接触，甚至还有一些煽动者的加入，

sentences.en: makes it really clear that something was about to happen.
sentences.zh: 让人非常清楚地意识到有事情要发生了。

sentences.en: And what was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么事？

sentences.en: What ended up happening?
sentences.zh: 最终发生了什么？

sentences.en: On Monday night, a group of about 60 counter-protesters tried to breach the encampment there, and the campus police had to break it up.
sentences.zh: 周一晚上，大约有60名反抗议者试图突破那里的营地，校园警察不得不介入制止。

sentences.en: And things escalated again on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 周二局势再次升级。

sentences.en: They stormed the barricades, and it's a complete riot.
sentences.zh: 他们冲破了路障，现场彻底成了一场骚乱。

sentences.en: I went to report on what happened just a few hours after it ended.
sentences.zh: 就在冲突结束后几个小时，我去报道了现场的情况。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: And I spoke to a lot of protesters, and I met one demonstrator, Marie.
sentences.zh: 我采访了许多抗议者，我遇到了其中一位示威者，玛丽。

sentences.en: Yeah, my first name is Marie, M-A-R-I-E, last name's Salem.
sentences.zh: 对，我名叫玛丽，M-A-R-I-E，姓是萨利姆。

sentences.en: And are you a UCLA student?
sentences.zh: 你是加州大学洛杉矶分校的学生吗？

sentences.en: I'm a UCLA grad student.
sentences.zh: 我是加州大学洛杉矶分校的研究生。

sentences.en: And Marie described what happened.
sentences.zh: 接着玛丽描述了当时发生的事情。

sentences.en: So can you just tell me a little bit about what happened last night?
sentences.zh: 你能给我讲讲昨晚到底发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Last night, we were approached by, you know, over 100 counter-protesters who were very mobilized and ready to break into camp.
sentences.zh: 昨晚，我们遭到了一百多名反抗议者的接近，你知道的，他们动员得很充分，准备闯入营地。

sentences.en: They proceeded to try to breach our barricades extremely violently.
sentences.zh: 他们开始极其暴力地试图突破我们的路障。

sentences.en: Marie said it started getting out of hand when counter-protesters started setting off fireworks towards the camp.
sentences.zh: 玛丽说，当反抗议者开始向营地发射烟花时，局势开始失控。

sentences.en: They had bear spray.
sentences.zh: 他们有防熊喷雾。

sentences.en: They had mace.
sentences.zh: 他们有梅斯催泪喷雾。

sentences.en: They were throwing wood, kind of like spears, throwing water bottles, continuing fireworks.
sentences.zh: 他们像掷长矛一样投掷木棍，扔水瓶，还不断放烟花。

sentences.en: So she said that they were terrified.
sentences.zh: 所以她说他们当时吓坏了。

sentences.en: It was just all hands on deck.
sentences.zh: 简直是全员出动。

sentences.en: Everyone was guarding the barricades.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在守卫路障。

sentences.en: Every time someone was experiencing the bear spray or a mace or was hit and bleeding, we had some medics in the front line, and then we had people.
sentences.zh: 每当有人吸入防熊喷雾或催泪瓦斯，或者被打伤流血时，我们前线有一些医务人员，然后还有其他人。

sentences.en: And they said that they were just trying to take care of people who were injured.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们只是在努力照顾受伤的人。

sentences.en: I mean, at any given moment, there is, you know, five to ten people being treated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在任何特定时刻，都有五到十个人在接受治疗。

sentences.en: So what you described to me sounded more like a battlefield than a college campus.
sentences.zh: 所以你向我描述的情景听起来更像是一个战场，而不是大学校园。

sentences.en: And it was just a complete terror and complete abandonment of the university, as we also watched private security watch this the entire time on the stairs.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场彻头彻尾的恐怖，也是大学的彻底失职，我们还看到私人安保人员全程坐在台阶上看着这一切。

sentences.en: And some LAPD were stationed about a football field length back from these counter-protesters
sentences.zh: 一些洛杉矶警察局的警察驻扎在距离这些反抗议者大约一个美式足球场长度的地方，

sentences.en: and did not make a single arrest, did not attempt to stop any violence, did not attempt to get in between the two groups.
sentences.zh: 却没有实施一次逮捕，没有试图阻止任何暴力行为，也没有试图介入两拨人中间。

sentences.en: No attempt.
sentences.zh: 毫无作为。

sentences.en: I should say, I spoke to state authorities and eyewitnesses, and they confirmed Marie's account about what happened that night,
sentences.zh: 我必须说明的是，我采访了州政府官员和目击者，他们证实了玛丽关于那天晚上所发生事情的说法，

sentences.en: both in terms of the violence that took place at the encampment and how law enforcement responded.
sentences.zh: 无论是营地发生的暴力事件，还是执法部门的反应，都是如此。

sentences.en: So in the end, people ended up fighting for hours before the police intervened.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，双方激战了几个小时，警察才介入。

sentences.en: So in her mind, UCLA's hands-off approach, which seemed to have prevailed throughout this entire period, ends up being way too hands-off in a moment when students were in jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 所以在她看来，加州大学洛杉矶分校在整个时期似乎一直采取的这种“不干涉”政策，在学生处于危险之中的时刻，未免变得太过于放任不管了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And so at this point, the protesters in the encampment started preparing for sort of two possibilities.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，营地里的抗议者开始为两种可能性做准备。

sentences.en: One was that this group of counter-protesters would return and attack them.
sentences.zh: 一种是这群反抗议者会卷土重来攻击他们。

sentences.en: And the second one was that the police would come and try to break up this encampment.
sentences.zh: 另一种是警察会来试图清场。

sentences.en: So they start building up the barricades.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始加固路障。

sentences.en: They start reinforcing them with wood.
sentences.zh: 他们开始用木头加固路障。

sentences.en: And during the day, hundreds of people came and brought them supplies.
sentences.zh: 白天的时候，成百上千的人前来为他们运送物资。

sentences.en: They brought food.
sentences.zh: 他们送来了食物。

sentences.en: They brought helmets, goggles, earplugs, saline solution, all sort of things these people could use to defend themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们送来了头盔、护目镜、耳塞、生理盐水，以及各种这些人可以用来保护自己的东西。

sentences.en: And so they're really getting ready to burrow in.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的是在准备坚守阵地。

sentences.en: And in the end, it was the police who came.
sentences.zh: 最后来的却是警察。

sentences.en: So Wednesday at 7 p.m., they made an announcement on top of Voice Hall, which overlooks the encampment.
sentences.zh: 于是在周三晚上7点，他们在俯瞰营地的罗伊斯大楼顶上发布了公告。

sentences.en: Administrative criminal actions up to...
sentences.zh: 行政犯罪行为最高可达……

sentences.en: And they told people in the encampment that they needed to leave or face arreSt.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉营地里的人必须离开，否则将面临逮捕。

sentences.en: And so as night falls, they put on all this gear that they've been collecting, the goggles, the masks, and the earplugs, and they wait for the police.
sentences.zh: 随着夜幕降临，他们戴上了收集来的所有装备——护目镜、面具和耳塞，等待警察的到来。

sentences.en: And so the police arrive and sort of station themselves right in front of the encampment.
sentences.zh: 警察随后抵达，并在营地正前方驻扎下来。

sentences.en: And then at a certain point, they stormed the back stairs of the encampment.
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时刻，他们冲向了营地的后方台阶。

sentences.en: And this is the stairs that the protesters started using to enter and exit the camp.
sentences.zh: 这就是抗议者们开始用来进出营地的那些台阶。

sentences.en: And they set up a line.
sentences.zh: 他们拉起了一条防线。

sentences.en: And the protesters do this really surprising thing.
sentences.zh: 而抗议者们做了一件非常令人惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: They open up umbrellas.
sentences.zh: 他们撑开了雨伞。

sentences.en: They have these sort of strobe lights.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着这种频闪灯。

sentences.en: And they're flashing them at the police, who sort of just like slowly back out of the camp.
sentences.zh: 他们把灯光闪向警察，警察则有点像是在慢慢撤出营地。

sentences.en: And so at this point, they're feeling really great.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一刻，他们感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: You know, they're like, we did it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们会觉得，我们做到了。

sentences.en: We pushed them out of the camp.
sentences.zh: 我们把他们赶出营地了。

sentences.en: And when the cops try to push again on those same set of stairs...
sentences.zh: 当警察试图再次从那组台阶强行推进时……

sentences.en: Hold your ground!
sentences.zh: 坚守阵地！

sentences.en: The protesters organize themselves with all these shields that they had built earlier.
sentences.zh: 抗议者们用他们之前制作的所有盾牌组织起防线。

sentences.en: And they go and confront them.
sentences.zh: 他们上前与警察对峙。

sentences.en: And so there's this moment where the police are trying to push up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 于是出现了这样一个时刻：警察试图往台阶上冲。

sentences.en: And the protesters are literally pushing them back.
sentences.zh: 而抗议者们则硬生生地把他们推了回去。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, dozens of the police officers who were there basically just turn around and leave.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，现场的数十名警员基本上直接转身离开了。

sentences.en: So how does this eventually come to an end?
sentences.zh: 那么这最终是如何结束的呢？

sentences.en: So at a certain point, the police push in again.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，警察再次强行突入。

sentences.en: Most of the conflict is centered at the front of these barricades.
sentences.zh: 大部分冲突集中在这些路障的前方。

sentences.en: And the police just start tearing them apart.
sentences.zh: 警察开始直接把路障拆毁。

sentences.en: They remove the front barricade.
sentences.zh: 他们拆除了正面的路障。

sentences.en: And in its place is this group of protesters who have linked arMs.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是一群手臂挽着手臂的抗议者。

sentences.en: And they're hanging on to each other.
sentences.zh: 他们紧紧依偎在一起。

sentences.en: And the police are trying to pull protesters one by one away from this group.
sentences.zh: 警察正试图把抗议者从这群人中一个接一个地拉开。

sentences.en: But they're having a really hard time because there's so many protesters.
sentences.zh: 但他们觉得非常艰难，因为抗议者实在太多了。

sentences.en: And they're all just hanging on to each other.
sentences.zh: 而且他们都紧紧抓着彼此。

sentences.en: So at a certain point, one of the police officers started firing something into the crowd.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，其中一名警察开始向人群中发射某种东西。

sentences.en: We don't exactly know what it was.
sentences.zh: 我们不确定那具体是什么。

sentences.en: But it really spooked the protesters.
sentences.zh: 但这确实吓坏了抗议者。

sentences.en: Stop shooting at me!
sentences.zh: 别向我开枪！

sentences.en: Stop shooting at me!
sentences.zh: 别向我开枪！

sentences.en: They started falling back.
sentences.zh: 他们开始往后退。

sentences.en: Everyone was really scared.
sentences.zh: 每个人都非常害怕。

sentences.en: The protesters were yelling, don't shoot us.
sentences.zh: 抗议者在大喊，别朝我们开枪。

sentences.en: And at that point, the police just sort of stormed the camp.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，警察直接冲进了营地。

sentences.en: Get back!
sentences.zh: 退后！

sentences.en: Get back!
sentences.zh: 退后！

sentences.en: Get back!
sentences.zh: 退后！

sentences.en: Get back!
sentences.zh: 退后！

sentences.en: And so after about four hours of this, the police pushed the protesters out of the encampment.
sentences.zh: 所以在经历了大约四个小时的对峙后，警察把抗议者赶出了营地。

sentences.en: They had arrested about 200 protesters.
sentences.zh: 他们逮捕了大约200名抗议者。

sentences.en: And this was finally over.
sentences.zh: 这场风波终于结束了。

sentences.en: And I'm just curious, Jonathan, because you're standing right there.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我很好奇，因为你当时就站在那里。

sentences.en: You are bearing witness to this all.
sentences.zh: 你亲历了这一切。

sentences.en: What you're thinking, what your impressions of this were.
sentences.zh: 你在想什么，你对此有什么印象。

sentences.en: I mean, I was stunned.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我惊呆了。

sentences.en: These are mostly teenagers.
sentences.zh: 这些人大多是十几岁的青少年。

sentences.en: This is a college campus, an institution of higher learning.
sentences.zh: 这是一所大学校园，一座高等学府。

sentences.en: And what I saw in front of me looked like a war zone.
sentences.zh: 而我眼前所见看起来就像战区。

sentences.en: The massive barricade, the police coming in with riot gear.
sentences.zh: 巨大的路障，全副防暴装备进场的警察。

sentences.en: And all this violence was happening in front of these red brick buildings that are famous for symbolizing a really open college campus.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些暴力事件，就发生在这些红砖建筑前，这些建筑可是象征着极其开放的大学校园的标志。

sentences.en: And everything about it was just totally surreal.
sentences.zh: 这一切都显得极其超现实。

sentences.en: Well, Jonathan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，乔纳森，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“拼字蜂”和“字谜”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的。

sentences.en: Like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏。

sentences.en: Peter, around 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 彼得，大约上午10点。

sentences.en: on Thursday morning, as the smoke is literally still clearing at the
sentences.zh: 在周四上午，当硝烟味实际上还在

sentences.en: University of California, Los Angeles, you get word that President Biden is going to speak.
sentences.zh: 加州大学洛杉矶分校弥漫时，你得到了拜登总统将要发表讲话的消息。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: It wasn't on his public schedule.
sentences.zh: 这并不在他的公开日程上。

sentences.en: He was about to head to Andrews Air Force Base in order to take a trip.
sentences.zh: 他正准备前往安德鲁斯空军基地以便进行一次出行。

sentences.en: And then suddenly we got the notice that he was going to be addressing the cameras in the
sentences.zh: 然后突然我们接到通知，他将要在

sentences.en: Roosevelt Room.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福厅面对镜头发表讲话。

sentences.en: They didn't tell us what he was going to talk about, but it was pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 他们没有告诉我们他要谈论什么，但这相当明显。

sentences.en: I think everybody understood that it was going to be about these campus protests, about the
sentences.zh: 我想大家都明白，这将是关于这些校园抗议活动，关于

sentences.en: growing violence and the clashes with police and the arrests that the entire country had been watching on TV every night for the past week.
sentences.zh: 不断升级的暴力事件、与警察的冲突以及过去一周全国每晚都在电视上看到的逮捕行动。

sentences.en: And I think that we were watching just that morning with UCLA, and it reached the point where he just had to say something.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在那天早上正看着加州大学洛杉矶分校的情况，事情已经发展到他不得不说点什么的地步了。

sentences.en: And why, in his estimation and those of his advisors, was this the moment that Biden had to say something?
sentences.zh: 那么，在他和他的顾问们看来，为什么这是拜登必须说点什么的时刻呢？

sentences.en: Well, it kind of reached a boiling point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点达到了沸点。

sentences.en: It kind of reached the impression of a national crisis.
sentences.zh: 这给人一种国家危机爆发的印象。

sentences.en: And you expect to hear your president address it in this kind of a moment, particularly because it's about his own policy.
sentences.zh: 你期望你的总统在这样的时刻对此发表讲话，特别是当这涉及到他自己的政策时。

sentences.en: His policy toward Israel is at the heart of these protests.
sentences.zh: 他对以色列的政策正是这些抗议活动的核心。

sentences.en: And he was getting a lot of grief.
sentences.zh: 而且他遭到了很多责难。

sentences.en: He was getting a lot of grief from Republicans who were chiding him for not speaking out personally.
sentences.zh: 共和党人指责他没有亲自发声，这让他承受了很大压力。

sentences.en: He hadn't said anything in about 10 days.
sentences.zh: 他已经有大约10天没说过话了。

sentences.en: He's got a lot of pressure from Democrats, too, who wanted him to come out and be more forceful.
sentences.zh: 民主党人也给他施加了很大压力，他们希望他出来表现得更强硬。

sentences.en: It wasn't enough in their view to leave it to his spokespeople to say something.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，把事情留给他的发言人去表态是不够的。

sentences.en: Moderate Democrats felt he needed to come out and take some leadership on this.
sentences.zh: 温和派民主党人认为他需要站出来，在这件事上发挥领导作用。

sentences.en: And so at the appointed moment, Peter, what does Biden actually say in the Roosevelt Room of the White House?
sentences.zh: 所以在指定的时刻，彼得，拜登在白宫的罗斯福厅究竟说了什么？

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Before I head to North Carolina, I wanted to speak for a few moments about what's going on on our college campuses here.
sentences.zh: 在我前往北卡罗来纳州之前，我想花几分钟时间谈谈我们这里大学校园里正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Well, he comes into the Roosevelt Room and he talks to the camera.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他走进罗斯福厅，对着镜头讲话。

sentences.en: He talks about the two clashing imperatives of American principle.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了美国原则中两个相互冲突的迫切需求。

sentences.en: The first is the right to free speech and for people to peacefully assemble and make their voices heard.
sentences.zh: 首先是言论自由的权利，以及人们和平集会并发出自己声音的权利。

sentences.en: The second is the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 第二个是法治。

sentences.en: Both must be upheld.
sentences.zh: 两者都必须维护。

sentences.en: One is freedom of speech.
sentences.zh: 一个是言论自由。

sentences.en: The other is the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 另一个是法治。

sentences.en: In fact, peaceful protest is in the best tradition of how Americans respond to consequential issues.
sentences.zh: 事实上，和平抗议是美国人应对重大问题时最好的传统方式。

sentences.en: But, but, neither are we a lawless country.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，我们也不是一个无法无天的国家。

sentences.en: In other words, what he's saying is, yes, I support the right of these protesters to come and object to even my own policy, in effect, is what he's saying, but it shouldn't trail
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他想表达的是，是的，我支持这些抗议者前来反对甚至是我自己的政策，实际上他说的就是这个，但它不应该演变成

sentences.en: into violence.
sentences.zh: 暴力。

sentences.en: Destroying property is not a peaceful proteSt.
sentences.zh: 破坏财产不是和平抗议。

sentences.en: It's against the law.
sentences.zh: 这是违法的。

sentences.en: Vandalism.
sentences.zh: 蓄意破坏。

sentences.en: Trespassing.
sentences.zh: 擅闯。

sentences.en: Breaking windows.
sentences.zh: 砸碎窗户。

sentences.en: Shutting down campuses.
sentences.zh: 关闭校园。

sentences.en: It shouldn't trail into taking over buildings and obstructing students from going to class or canceling their graduations.
sentences.zh: 它不应该演变成占领建筑物、阻碍学生去上课或取消他们的毕业典礼。

sentences.en: Threatening people, intimidating people, instilling fear in people is not peaceful proteSt.
sentences.zh: 威胁他人、恐吓他人、在人们心中制造恐惧不是和平抗议。

sentences.en: It's against the law.
sentences.zh: 这是违法的。

sentences.en: And he leans very heavily into this idea that what he's seeing these days goes beyond the line.
sentences.zh: 他非常强调这样一个观点，即他如今所看到的已经越过了红线。

sentences.en: I understand people have strong feelings and deep convictions.
sentences.zh: 我理解人们有强烈的感情和深厚的信念。

sentences.en: In America, we respect the right and protect the right for them to express that.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们尊重并保护他们表达这一点的权利。

sentences.en: But it doesn't mean anything goes.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着可以为所欲为。

sentences.en: It is crossed into harassment and expressions of hate in a way that go against the national character.
sentences.zh: 这已经跨越到了骚扰和仇恨言论的地步，违背了国民性格。

sentences.en: As president, I will always defend free speech.
sentences.zh: 作为总统，我将永远捍卫言论自由。

sentences.en: And I will always be just as strong as standing up for the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 我也将永远坚定地捍卫法治。

sentences.en: That's my responsibility to you, the American people, my obligation to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这是我对你们美国人民的责任，我对宪法的义务。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As I watched the speech, I heard his overriding message to basically be, I, the president of the United States, I'm drawing a line.
sentences.zh: 当我观看这段演讲时，我听到他最核心的信息基本上是，我，美利坚合众国总统，我正在划一条红线。

sentences.en: These protests and counter-protests, you know, the seizing and defacing of campus buildings,
sentences.zh: 这些抗议和反抗议活动，你们知道的，占领和损毁校园建筑、

sentences.en: class disruption, all of it, name-calling, it's getting out of hand that there's a right way to do this.
sentences.zh: 扰乱课堂、所有这一切、辱骂，已经失控了，正确做事是有方法的。

sentences.en: And what I'm seeing is the wrong way to do it.
sentences.zh: 而我看到的则是错误的做法。

sentences.en: And it has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这必须停止。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And as he's wrapping up, reporters, of course, ask questions.
sentences.zh: 就在他快要结束时，记者们当然会提问。

sentences.en: And the first question is,
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是，

sentences.en: Mr. President, have the protests forced you to reconsider any of the policies with regard to the region?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，抗议活动是否迫使您重新考虑对该地区的任何政策？

sentences.en: Will this change your policy toward the war in Gaza?
sentences.zh: 这会改变你对加沙战争的政策吗？

sentences.en: Which, of course, is exactly what the protesters want.
sentences.zh: 而这，当然正是抗议者想要的。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 关键就在这里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he basically says,
sentences.zh: 基本上他的回答是，

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Just one word, no.
sentences.zh: 只有一个字，不。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that felt kind of important, as brief and fleeting as it was, because at the end of the day, what he's saying to these protesters is, I'm not going to do what you want.
sentences.zh: 尽管这简短而短暂，但感觉相当重要，因为归根结底，他对这些抗议者说的是，我不会按你们的意愿行事。

sentences.en: And basically, your protests are never going to work.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你们的抗议是永远不会起作用的。

sentences.en: I'm not going to change the U.S.'s involvement in this war.
sentences.zh: 我不会改变美国对这场战争的介入。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: He is saying, you know, I'm not going to be swayed by angry people in the streets.
sentences.zh: 他是在说，你知道，我不会被街头愤怒的人群左右。

sentences.en: I'm going to do what I think is right when it comes to foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 在涉及外交政策时，我只会做我认为正确的事。

sentences.en: Now, what he thinks is that they're not giving him enough credit for trying to achieve what they want, which is an end of the war.
sentences.zh: 现在，他认为他们没有给予他足够的赞赏，因为他一直在努力实现他们想要的，也就是结束战争。

sentences.en: He has been pressuring Israel and Hamas to come to a deal for a ceasefire that hopefully, in his view, would then lead to a more enduring end of hostilities.
sentences.zh: 他一直在向以色列和哈马斯施压，要求达成停火协议，在他看来，这有望随后带来更持久的敌对状态结束。

sentences.en: But, of course, this deal hasn't gone anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这个协议毫无进展。

sentences.en: Hamas, in particular, seems to be resisting it.
sentences.zh: 尤其是哈马斯，似乎在抵制它。

sentences.en: And so the president is left with a policy of arming Israel without having found a way yet to stop the war.
sentences.zh: 因此，总统只能采取武装以色列的政策，而尚未找到制止战争的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I wonder, though, Peter, if we're being honest, don't these protests, despite what Biden is saying there, inevitably exert a kind of power over him, you know, becoming one of
sentences.zh: 不过彼得，说句实话，我很好奇，尽管拜登这么说，这些抗议活动难道不会不可避免地对他施加某种权力吗，你知道的，它成为了众多压力之一，但无论如何这种压力确实影响了他对这些时刻的看法。

sentences.en: many pressures, but a pressure nonetheless that does influence how he thinks about these moments.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他现在在白宫，把与全国的整场对话都用来讨论这些校园抗议活动。

sentences.en: I mean, here he is at the White House devoting an entire conversation to the nation to these campus protests.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，他知道这滋养了他竞选连任的政治环境，

sentences.en: Well, look, he knows this feeds into the political environment in which he's running for re-election,
sentences.zh: 在这种环境中，他基本上失去了原本可能是他左翼支持者的支持，他们对感到他失望。

sentences.en: in which he basically has people who otherwise might be his supporters on the left disenchanted with him.
sentences.zh: 而且他知道这是要付出代价的。

sentences.en: And he knows that there's a cost to be paid.
sentences.zh: 当他在思考该怎么做时，这显然浮现在他的脑海中。

sentences.en: And that certainly obviously is in his head as he's thinking about what to do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他对手战争的看法由于各种原因每天都在改变，其中大部分与地面现实有关。

sentences.en: But I think his view of the war is changing by the day for all sorts of reasons, and most of them having to do with realities on the ground.
sentences.zh: 他已经认定以色列在加沙开展此次行动的方式已经走得够远，甚至可以说是过头了。

sentences.en: He has decided that Israel has gone far enough, if not too far, in the way it has conducted this operation in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 他对那里的人道主义危机感到不安，并正在寻找一种方法，将这一切打包成一种迈向和平制造的举措，比如开始让该地区

sentences.en: He is upset about the humanitarian crisis there, and he's looking for a way to wrap all this up into kind of a move that would move to peacemaking, like beginning to get the region
sentences.zh: 进入一个不同的阶段，也许与沙特阿拉伯达成一项协议，以实现与以色列关系正常化，

sentences.en: to a different stage, maybe have a deal with the Saudis to normalize relations with Israel
sentences.zh: 作为交换，达成某种最终从根本上解决巴勒斯坦问题的两国方案。

sentences.en: in exchange for some sort of a two-state solution that would eventually resolve the Palestinian issue at its core.
sentences.zh: 所以我想可以公平地说，抗议活动不会在直接意义上撼动他，但它们显然融入了当下的更大时代精神中。

sentences.en: So I think it's probably fair to say that the protests won't move him in an immediate kind of sense, but they obviously play into the larger zeitgeist of the moment.
sentences.zh: 我也认为了解乔金·拜登的本质很重要。

sentences.en: And I also think it's important to know who Joe Biden is at heart.
sentences.zh: 详细解释一下。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 他不是被动主义吸引的那种人。

sentences.en: He's not drawn to activism.
sentences.zh: 例如，1968年我们上次看到哥伦比亚大学发生这种重大动乱时，他就在周围。

sentences.en: He was around in 1968, the last time we saw this major conflagration at Columbia University, for instance.
sentences.zh: 当时，乔·拜登是锡拉丘兹大学的一名法科学生，距离大约250英里远。

sentences.en: At the time, Joe Biden was a law student in Syracuse, about 250 miles away.
sentences.zh: 当时，乔·拜登是雪城大学的一名法学院学生，距离大约有250英里。

sentences.en: And he was an institutionalist even then.
sentences.zh: 而且他那时就已经是个体制内的人了。

sentences.en: He was just focused on his studies.
sentences.zh: 他当时只专注于学业。

sentences.en: He was about to graduate.
sentences.zh: 他正准备毕业。

sentences.en: He was thinking about the law career.
sentences.zh: 他当时在考虑法律职业。

sentences.en: And he didn't really have much of an affinity, I think, for his fellow students of that era for their activist way of looking at things.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他对他那个时代的同学们那种充满激进主义的看问题方式，其实并没有什么好感。

sentences.en: He tells a story in his memoir about walking down the street in Syracuse one day to go to the pizza shop with some friends.
sentences.zh: 他在回忆录里讲了一个故事：有一天，他在锡拉丘兹的街头散步，和几个朋友一起去披萨店。

sentences.en: And they walk by the administration building, and they see people hanging out of the windows.
sentences.zh: 他们路过行政大楼时，看到有人把身子挂在窗户外面。

sentences.en: They're hanging SDS banners.
sentences.zh: 他们在悬挂SDS的横幅。

sentences.en: That's the Students for a Democratic Society, which was one of the big activist groups of the era.
sentences.zh: 那是“争取民主社会学生组织”，是那个时代最大的激进组织之一。

sentences.en: And he says, they were taking over the building, and we looked up and said, look at those assholes.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们当时正在接管大楼，我们抬头一看说，瞧瞧那些混蛋。

sentences.en: That's how far apart from the anti-war movement I was.
sentences.zh: 这就是我与反战运动的距离。

sentences.en: That's him writing in his memoir.
sentences.zh: 这是他在回忆录中写的。

sentences.en: So to a young Joe Biden, those who devote their time and their energy to protesting the war are, I don't need to repeat the word twice, but they're losers.
sentences.zh: 所以对于年轻的乔·拜登来说，那些把时间和精力奉献给抗议战争的人，我不需要重复那个词，但他们就是失败者。

sentences.en: They're not worth his time.
sentences.zh: 他们不值得他浪费时间。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's the tactics they're using more than the goals that he disagreed with.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为他不同意的是他们采用的战术，而不是他们的目标。

sentences.en: He would tell you he disagreed with the Vietnam War, he was for civil rights, but he thought
sentences.zh: 他会告诉你他不同意越南战争，他支持民权运动，但他认为

sentences.en: that taking over a building was performative, was all about getting attention, and that there was a better way, in his view, to do it.
sentences.zh: 占领大楼是在作秀，完全是为了博取眼球，而在他看来，有更好的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: He was somebody who wanted to work inside the system.
sentences.zh: 他是一个想要在体制内工作的人。

sentences.en: He said in an interview quite a few years back, he says, look, I was wearing sports coats in that era.
sentences.zh: 他很多年前在一次采访中说过，听着，那个时代我都是穿着运动西装的。

sentences.en: He saw himself becoming part of the system, not somebody trying to tear it down.
sentences.zh: 他把自己视为体制的一部分，而不是那种试图摧毁体制的人。

sentences.en: And so how should we think about that Joe Biden when we think about this Joe Biden?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们思考现在的这个乔·拜登时，我们应该如何看待当年的那个乔·拜登呢？

sentences.en: I mean, the Joe Biden who, as a young man, looked upon anti-war protesters with disdain, and the one who is now president, and his very own policies have inspired such ferocious
sentences.zh: 我是说，那个年轻时对反战示威者满怀鄙视的乔·拜登，和现在身为总统、而他自己的政策却引发了如此狂热的

sentences.en: campus protests.
sentences.zh: 校园抗议的乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, that Joe Biden, the 1968 Joe Biden, he could just throw on his sports coat, go to the pizza shop with his friends, make fun of the activists and call them names,
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，那个乔·拜登，1968年的乔·拜登，他可以随便套上一件运动西装，和朋友去披萨店，嘲笑那些激进分子并给他们起外号，

sentences.en: and then that's it.
sentences.zh: 然后就没事了。

sentences.en: They didn't have to affect his life.
sentences.zh: 那些事不会影响他的生活。

sentences.en: But that's not what 2024 Joe Biden can do.
sentences.zh: 但2024年的乔·拜登可不能这样做。

sentences.en: Now, wherever he goes, he's dogged by this.
sentences.zh: 现在，无论他走到哪里，都饱受这方面的纠缠。

sentences.en: He goes to speeches, and people are shouting at him, genocide Joe, genocide Joe.
sentences.zh: 他去发表演讲，人们冲他大喊，种族灭绝乔，种族灭绝乔。

sentences.en: He is the target of the same kind of a movement that he disdained in 1968.
sentences.zh: 他成了他曾在1968年所鄙视的那类运动的目标。

sentences.en: And so as much as he would like to ignore it or move on or focus on other things, I think this has become a defining image of his year.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管他很想忽视它、抛之脑后或专注于其他事情，但我认为这已经成为他这一年最具代表性的形象。

sentences.en: And one of the defining images, perhaps, of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 也许也是他总统任期内最具代表性的形象之一。

sentences.en: And 2024 Joe Biden can't simply ignore it.
sentences.zh: 而2024年的乔·拜登不能简单地忽视它。

sentences.en: Well, Peter, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，彼得，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: During testimony on Thursday in Donald Trump's hush money trial, jurors heard a recording
sentences.zh: 在周四对唐纳德·特朗普封口费案的作证中，陪审团听取了一段

sentences.en: secretly made by Trump's former fixer, Michael Cohen, in which Trump discusses a deal to buy a woman's silence.
sentences.zh: 由特朗普的前密友迈克尔·科恩秘密录制的录音，录音中特朗普讨论了一笔购买某女性沉默的交易。

sentences.en: In the recording, Trump asks Cohen about how one payment made by Trump to a woman named
sentences.zh: 在录音中，特朗普向科恩询问关于特朗普向一名叫

sentences.en: Karen McDougal would be financed.
sentences.zh: 凯伦·麦克杜格尔的女性支付的一笔款项将如何筹措。

sentences.en: The recording could complicate efforts by Trump's lawyers to distance him from the hush money deals at the center of the trial.
sentences.zh: 这段录音可能会让特朗普的律师们试图将他与案件中心的封口费交易撇清关系的努力变得复杂。

sentences.en: A final thing to know.
sentences.zh: 最后一件需要了解的事。

sentences.zh: 明天早上，我们将向你发送我们的同事在

sentences.zh: 本周，大卫·马尔凯斯与喜剧明星马龙·韦恩斯就他的新单口喜剧专场进行了交谈。

sentences.en: It's a high that you get when you don't know if this joke that I'm about to say is going to offend everybody, or they're going to walk out, or they're going to boo me, or they're
sentences.zh: 当你不知道我接下来要讲的这个笑话会不会冒犯所有人，或者他们会不会离场、会不会嘘我、会不会

sentences.en: going to hate this.
sentences.zh: 讨厌这个时，你会获得一种高潮般的快感。

sentences.en: And then you tell it, and everybody cracks up, and you're like, whew!
sentences.zh: 然后你讲出来了，所有人都哄堂大笑，你会想，呼！

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
